rich_summary: On Mount Rishyamuka, the exiled monkey king Sugriva spots the armed princes Rama and Lakshmana approaching the forest. Terrified that his powerful brother Bali has sent assassins, Sugriva panics and flees from peak to peak with his monkey companions. His minister Hanuman calms him, arguing that Bali is nowhere nearby and urging clear judgment instead of fear. Sugriva, still wary of royal intrigue, decides caution is wiser than flight. He orders Hanuman to approach the strangers in disguise as a common man, observe their speech, gestures, and intentions, and win their trust through courtesy and praise. Thus begins the pivotal encounter that will unite Rama and the vanara kingdom—Hanuman’s first meeting with Rama, a moment that will spark the alliance leading to the search for Sita and the coming war with Ravana.

highlight_spans.why: The opening moment where Sugriva first beholds Rama and Lakshmana and reacts with fear, setting the tension for the encounter.
Sugriva’s panic and restless flight across the mountain reveal his trauma and fear of Bali.
Hanuman’s calming counsel highlights his wisdom and loyalty, foreshadowing his role as mediator between Rama and Sugriva.
Sugriva’s command that Hanuman approach the princes in disguise marks the decisive step that leads to Hanuman’s historic first meeting with Rama.

top_scenes.scene_text: Sugriva and a band of monkeys leap frantically from crag to crag on the high mountain as they glimpse the armed princes Rama and Lakshmana below in the forest.
Hanuman respectfully addresses the anxious Sugriva on the mountaintop, calming the monkey king while the wind sweeps through the high rocky peaks.
Hanuman prepares to descend the mountain in disguise to approach the radiant warriors Rama and Lakshmana standing with bows in the forest clearing.
